approval_required_for: Assigning a nonzero clock_target_mhz or changing board clock/reset/shell assumptions without cited board-profile or Vivado evidence.
Selecting app-shell target names, shell ports, or AXI/DDR integration points when backend target discovery evidence is ambiguous.
Any architecture, pipeline, memory-layout, numeric-policy, or major template change beyond bounded repair boundaries.
Changing numeric tolerance policy, golden-reference generation policy, or expected outputs.
Proceeding with deployment claims after any failed or missing real-tool checker evidence.

executable_actions.on_failure: Quarantine the candidate stage artifact, open a bounded stage_retry_request or trust barrier, and do not promote to verification/backend consumers.
executable_actions.rationale: Emit the stage acceptance decision and evidence matrix from visible pass evidence while recording that later functional, backend, and board checks remain unproven.

executable_actions.on_failure: Do not run real functional simulation; return the failed contract evidence to the orchestrator for bounded codegen/verification repair classification.
executable_actions.rationale: Downstream verification must convert the accepted codegen package into a checker-grounded hierarchical verification plan before real simulation or repair decisions.

executable_actions.on_failure: Classify the issue as checker/golden-reference/input-packing repair unless real RTL tool evidence identifies a hardware failure; do not alter tolerances or golden outputs without approved numeric-policy change.
executable_actions.rationale: Real functional and numerical checks require reproducible input, packed weight, golden-reference, and hash manifests derived from the accepted model/numeric/runtime contracts.

executable_actions.on_failure: Stop at the earliest failed layer; route simulator output through boundary-contract-guided localization and causal repair context, then rerun only the targeted failed checker before promotion.
executable_actions.rationale: Enforce the three-layer verification loop after static contract and real-weight gates: operator/leaf modules first, connected single-transformer-layer second, and no promotion beyond the first failing layer.

executable_actions.on_failure: Localize to the wrapper, runtime ABI, memory layout, or generated RTL boundary before any code repair; do not proceed to Vivado or board execution.
executable_actions.rationale: After leaf and single-layer verification pass, validate the board-accurate AXI/DDR wrapped system against memory layout, runtime config, protocol, order, and liveness constraints before backend synthesis.

executable_actions.on_failure: If target names, shell ports, memory interfaces, or clock evidence remain ambiguous, require bounded human/architecture approval and keep runtime bitstream and board runtime blocked.
executable_actions.rationale: Board/app-shell integration must be synthesized from cited board materials and real tool evidence; clock_target_mhz is currently unknown and must not be guessed.

executable_actions.on_failure: Route real Vivado evidence to backend bounded recovery or architecture review; do not bypass DRC/timing failures or represent them as code_generation pass evidence.
executable_actions.rationale: Vivado synthesis, implementation, and timing/resource reports are later-stage real-tool evidence and must not be inferred from Chisel compile/elaboration success.

executable_actions.on_failure: Localize the board/runtime/interface boundary using real tool output, then open bounded recovery or backtrack; do not claim hardware pass.
executable_actions.rationale: Only board runtime, runtime ABI, bitstream, and output-validity evidence can support a board-level pass claim.

proposed_actions: Promote the code_generation artifact to downstream verification/backend consumers with an explicit checker evidence matrix and repair-or-handoff boundary record.
In verification, first build the hierarchical verification artifact contract and boundary contracts from the accepted generated package, memory layout, runtime config, and SACG constraints.

Generate real-weight/golden-reference manifests and then run layered real-tool verification in order: operator/leaf modules, connected single-transformer-layer kernel, then board-accurate AXI/DDR wrapped system. Stop and localize on the first failed layer.
In backend_board, discover app-shell target names, shell ports, and board clock policy from cited board materials and real tool evidence; if ambiguous, require bounded approval rather than guessing.
Run Vivado synthesis/implementation/timing and board runtime/output-validity checks only after verification and backend target discovery gates pass.

If any later checker fails, open a localized retry/backtrack or trust-barrier record as appropriate; do not modify golden outputs, loosen tolerance, bypass checkers, or claim hardware pass without real tool evidence.
risks: Non-blocking later-stage risk: compile/elaboration and static contracts do not prove functional correctness, numerical tolerance compliance, liveness under real traffic, AXI/DDR protocol correctness, timing/resource closure, or board execution.

Non-blocking later-stage risk: memory_layout.json and runtime_config.json are accepted as codegen handoff artifacts, but Stage 6+ must validate address maps, transfer counts, DDR image roundtrip, and runtime ABI before deployment claims.

Non-blocking later-stage risk: clock_target_mhz=0 means the board shell clock is unknown; assigning a nonzero target or claiming timing closure requires board-profile/Vivado evidence or bounded approval.

Non-blocking process risk: any downstream failure must be localized at the earliest causal boundary and repaired through a bounded retry path; later stages must not skip from leaf/operator failure directly to board-level promotion.
